tasks.name: vector_two_broad
tasks.importance_reason: Basic learnable multimodal distribution and within-mode spread.
tasks.limitations: Finite-particle approximation; one initialization only.

tasks.name: vector_unequal_mass
tasks.importance_reason: Checks target occupancy including the rare 2% component, not uniformity.
tasks.limitations: Finite-particle approximation; one initialization only.

tasks.name: vector_unequal_width
tasks.importance_reason: Checks component-specific scales without imposing one shared Gaussian width.
tasks.limitations: Finite-particle approximation; one initialization only.

tasks.name: vector_anisotropic
tasks.importance_reason: Checks covariance shape: a narrow axis cannot be rescued by a wide one.
tasks.limitations: Finite-particle approximation; one initialization only.

tasks.name: vector_overlap
tasks.importance_reason: Scores the observable distribution when latent components are not identifiable.
tasks.limitations: Component labels and mode recall are deliberately not scored for overlapping densities.

tasks.name: vector_narrow
tasks.importance_reason: Deliberately narrow components test critic resolution; nonblocking diagnostic.
tasks.limitations: Fixed two-band Fourier critic is deliberately mismatched to sigma=.025; failure does not veto a controller.

tasks.name: vector_scale_drift
tasks.importance_reason: Tests adaptation to changing input units before a stationary final window.
tasks.limitations: Nonstationary diagnostic; each checkpoint uses the current target, which stops changing at 60% of budget.

tasks.name: vector_spiral
tasks.importance_reason: Checks continuous curved mass rather than a finite list of target mode centers.
tasks.limitations: Finite particles approximate a noisy spiral; sliced distances do not prove identical density.

tasks.name: reserved_annulus
tasks.importance_reason: Unseen rotationally symmetric continuous support and radial mass law.
tasks.limitations: Reserved family; no samples or evaluations are produced during calibration.

tasks.name: stress_fast_critic
tasks.importance_reason: A critic learning twice as fast is a realistic optimizer imbalance; maintaining distribution quality matters for routine tuning.
tasks.limitations: Changes only the critic learning rate; it does not test additional discriminator updates or minibatch changes.

tasks.name: stress_slow_critic
tasks.importance_reason: A critic learning half as fast tests whether feedback remains useful when generator transport can outrun density estimation.
tasks.limitations: The critic retains adequate architecture; failure within the fixed budget is not proof the target is unsolvable.

tasks.name: stress_small_batch
tasks.importance_reason: Batch 64 is an ordinary memory-limited setting; feedback should tolerate its noisier gradient observations.
tasks.limitations: The update count stays fixed, so this arm sees fewer training examples; report that compute/data difference rather than attributing everything to noise.

tasks.name: stress_large_critic
tasks.importance_reason: Doubling critic width is a plausible architecture choice that tests controller transfer across gradient scale and capacity.
tasks.limitations: A wider critic costs more per update; use wall time alongside update-normalized convergence.

tasks.name: stress_long_horizon
tasks.importance_reason: A doubled training horizon checks persistence of convergence and delayed collapse beyond the usual training budget.
tasks.limitations: There are still only 24 fixed observations, now 100 steps apart; stability between observations is not certified.

tasks.name: stress_r1_r2
tasks.importance_reason: A supported R1+R2 penalty tests whether a controller transfers across common discriminator regularization objectives.
tasks.limitations: Coefficient .1 is a predeclared reference alternative, not an equal-strength equivalence to the cap penalty or a search over coefficients.

tasks.name: stress_weak_critic
tasks.importance_reason: A deliberately narrow, shallow critic without Fourier features diagnoses an architecture bottleneck; this artificial weakness is not a selection requirement.
tasks.limitations: Failure can arise because the critic cannot resolve narrow target modes. It supplies diagnostic evidence only, even if another method succeeds.

tasks.name: stress_overlapping_data
tasks.importance_reason: Broad overlapping components diagnose sensitivity to ambiguous mixture labels. Distribution fit matters here; component reconstruction is not an appropriate requirement.
tasks.limitations: This intentionally blurred data is not representative of the separated-mode objective. Only global sliced distance is scored; HQ and component-mass/covariance claims are omitted.

tasks.name: reserved_alternating_critic_updates
tasks.importance_reason: A previously unseen discriminator update cadence tests transfer when opponent feedback arrives less often, rather than merely at a different learning rate.
tasks.limitations: Never evaluated in development. The target stays static; D updates every second outer step and G every step. Report both actual update counts and wall time because the work per outer step changes.

tasks.limitations: Finite 32-particle prior; 8x8 grayscale templates; no natural-image or stochastic-texture fidelity claim.

tasks.limitations: Finite 32-particle prior; 8x8 grayscale templates; no natural-image or stochastic-texture fidelity claim.

selection: Eligibility requires every required live test sustained. All required and ranking tests must be attempted before selection. Rank eligible rows by sustained pass fraction averaged equally across data, dynamics and image domains and equally across ranking families within each domain, then worst family fraction, then lower similarly balanced final metric shortfall, then lower confirmation/budget (failure=2). Shortfall is mean positive bound violation divided by abs(bound), with scale 1 for zero bounds and each metric capped at 2; invalid or missing results receive 2. Diagnostics never affect eligibility, score, or tie breaking. Errors are failures; missing attempts cannot improve rank. EMA never affects selection.
evidence: Importance is declared before candidate search; reference solvability is reported independently. Transfer predictiveness of each individual test has not been established.

search.screening: Run all nine required tests first; do not fit additional tasks after a required failure.
search.validation: Advance the two best eligible nonzero fitting policies and the cosine control to all image cases.
search.freeze: Choose full-development winner and best eligible nonzero challenger after validation. Evaluate one frozen challenger, its bias-only ablation, and cosine on reserved families once.
